A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BIT research despite the changed title. All 25 pages in each version, including Appendices A–S, are available and support reliable comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original attempted- and imagined-speech decoding results, benchmark submissions, ablations, and representation and error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and reports an updated Brain-to-Text ’25 ensemble result in Table 2.

M1.justification: Appendices G–H change the ’25 ensemble merger from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4, operating on 29 encoders instead of 10. This revises one inference component; the transformer encoder, pretraining, phoneme training, audio-LLM integration, and contrastive objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same human and monkey pretraining data and attempted- and imagined-speech tasks. The Temmar et al. (2025) attribution replaces Hisham et al. (2024) for the already-described finger-movement dataset; it does not introduce new data.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–2, the encoder comparisons, and the LLM and projector ablations. GPT-4 replaces the proposed ensemble's merger rather than becoming an additional evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix H revises the ’25 ensemble configuration from 10 encoders to 29 and specifies GPT-4 merging. The ’24 configuration remains 10 encoders with GPT-3.5. Reported datasets, splits, holdout sizes, metrics, and other evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The decoder, feature, and projector ablations are retained, as are the representation analyses, decoding-error analyses, scaling curves, pretraining-data exclusions, and equal-data SL-versus-SSL control in the appendices.

E5.justification: Appendix H changes the reported number of differently seeded ’25 encoders from 10 to 29. These seeds supply an ensemble, rather than repeated estimates of evaluation uncertainty. No confidence intervals, significance tests, or additional uncertainty-reporting practices are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 and Section 5.1 replace the ’25 BIT Cascaded + Ensemble WER of 2.21% with 1.76%, now explicitly described as a public-leaderboard result. Because the ensemble size and merger change, this is not a same-setting performance gain. Other reported values, including the end-to-end ensemble's 7.76%, are retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives, including the symmetric contrastive loss and combined training loss in Appendices I–J, are unchanged. No new assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or substantive derivations appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 6 retain the same claims about cross-species pretraining, benchmark leadership, improved end-to-end decoding, and cross-task alignment. The new title foregrounds the existing cross-species model without changing these scientific claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies the ’25 comparison as a public-leaderboard comparison and removes Appendix H's ongoing-competition explanation for reporting only supplied baselines. Mechanism interpretations and the substantive limitations concerning online decoding, latency, data availability, and transfer remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices G–H revise the implementation account to distinguish GPT-3.5 merging for ’24 from GPT-4 merging of 29 models for ’25. Other hyperparameter tables, hardware and training descriptions, preprocessing instructions, and data-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The new Temmar et al. (2025) bibliography entry completes and updates the attribution of the same dataset already cited as Hisham et al. (2024). Related-work discussion and substantive positioning against earlier research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Decoding inner speech with an end-to-end brain-to-text neural interface' to 'A cross-species neural foundation model for end-to-end speech decoding.' Conference headers, dataset attribution, and short passages in Section 5.1 and Appendices G–H are updated; the overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's dataset citation label is corrected, with small front-matter and reference-page layout adjustments. Figures, table structures, axes, and legends otherwise remain unchanged; Table 2's numerical replacement is assessed under E6.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves reporting precision through explicit public-leaderboard qualification, benchmark-specific ensemble documentation, and a complete reference for an existing dataset. The lower Table 2 WER accompanies a larger ensemble and different merger, so it does not establish a controlled performance improvement. The core scientific evidence and limitations remain essentially unchanged.
